title: Interplay between Interlayer Shift and Twist: Twisted van der Waals Nanowires Driven by Rotational Twinning
authors: Dong-gyu Kim, Kisung Kang, Hani Kang, Kihyun Lee, Yangjin Lee, Jinsub Park, Joong-Eon Jung, Min Kim, Myeongjin Jang, Aloysius Soon, Kwanpyo Kim
abstract: In van der Waals(vdW) layered materials, interlayer shift and twist have enabled the control of material properties through polytype and moire engineering. Various approaches, including bottom-up synthesis and manual layer-by-layer stacking, have been utilized to engineer targeted stacking configurations. However, the interplay between interlayer shift and twist, as well as reliable mechanisms for fine-tuning these parameters, remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a previously unrecognized twisting mechanism arising from preferred tilted stacking and twinning in vdW crystals. Electron diffraction and atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy(STEM) imaging reveal that the lattice planes of group-IV chalcogenide GeSe_{2-x}Te_x rotate continuously along the nanowire growth axis, with twist rates depending systematically on nanowire radius. Atomic-scale imaging further identifies a continuous rotational twin boundary extending along the central region of the nanowire. First-principles calculations and structural relaxation simulations confirm that the twisting deformation originates from energetic competition between the preferred interlayer stacking registry and the strain cost imposed by rotational twinning. These findings establish rotational twinning as an intrinsic route to spontaneous twist formation and provide a design principle for realizing twist-engineered vdW crystals with compatible crystal symmetries and stacking motifs.
summary: This work investigates the structural control in van der Waals nanowires, focusing on the interplay between interlayer shift and twist. The researchers identify and characterize a novel twisting mechanism driven by rotational twinning in GeSe2-xTe_x. This establishes rotational twinning as a fundamental, intrinsic method for engineering twist in these layered materials.
main_problem: The interplay between interlayer shift and twist in van der Waals (vdW) layered materials, and reliable mechanisms for fine-tuning these parameters, remain largely unexplored.
main_result: The authors report a previously unrecognized twisting mechanism in vdW crystals arising from preferred tilted stacking and rotational twinning, establishing this as an intrinsic route for spontaneous twist formation.
method: The study combines electron diffraction and atomic-resolution STEM imaging with first-principles calculations and structural relaxation simulations.
model_or_system: The physical system is group-IV chalcogenide GeSe2-xTe_x grown as nanowires, which exhibit continuous rotation of lattice planes along the growth axis.
key_observables: Continuous rotation of lattice planes, twist rates dependent on nanowire radius, and the presence of a continuous rotational twin boundary.

why_interesting: While focused on solid-state materials science, the concept of strain-induced structural transitions and emergent symmetries due to local interactions (twinning) has parallels in understanding quantum phase transitions or engineered quantum materials.
